cells.tense: Right now you are adjusting how the shared thing is held, and you can feel it happening.
cells.ask: Change one small thing in how you hand something down and watch whether it still lands. If it lands, keep the change.
cells.core: An adjustment is running and you can feel it — how much of this to carry forward, what to leave out, which version of it the room can take. You aren't the loudest one there and you aren't sitting it out. You're reading the moment and moving with it, and that is why what you offer comes across clean.\n\nHolding several things at once while staying present is what you're doing well. Nothing's frozen and nothing's slipping; you're calibrating. Keeping that costs something quiet — attention, most of it invisible on the far side. The ask is to shift one small thing and see whether it still lands. The doing is the evidence.
cells.sheetLine: You're adjusting how it lands, and it's landing.
cells.verb: sensing the adjustment that keeps a thing alive between people
cells.place: in the shared meaning a group carries forward

cells.tense: You will be working on the harmony of this before anyone has actually disagreed.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing you've been softening and say it plainly once, unanswered. Let the room hold it.
cells.core: You can feel the agreement arriving before it's real. Someone might push back, or the shape of this might change, so you smooth it now — ahead of time, before the actual moment shows up. The smoothing is well-meant and it's running early. You're not in the moment; you're a few turns in front of it, keeping the surface level.\n\nThe trouble is that the difference that needed to be made isn't getting made. Peace assembled before the disagreement is a room where the disagreement went underground. Keeping that costs you: nothing in the shared thing gets sharpened, and a lot of energy goes to a fight that hasn't arrived. The ask is to name the one thing you've been softening, once, and let the silence afterwards do what it does.
cells.sheetLine: You're making peace before anyone has disagreed.

cells.tense: You were standing in the door of it for a while and then you were somewhere else.
cells.ask: Say one true thing about what this shared thing means to you to one person, off-balance, and let that be the whole conversation.
cells.core: Every piece arrives on its own now — a ritual here, a phrase there, a half-finished sense of what it all added up to — and none of it holds still long enough to tune. You're not disengaged from meaning. You're scattered by everything that comes through, and nothing stays put long enough to be adjusted.\n\nMore input won't fix this. What's absent is the small steady centre that used to sit under all of it. Trying harder won't bring it back and feeling harder about it won't either — it returns sideways, through someone else. The ask is one true sentence to one person, out of balance, and letting that be enough.
cells.sheetLine: Plenty comes through. Nothing stays long enough to tune.

cells.tense: You are already tuning what gets shared, and you'd call it nothing in particular.
cells.ask: Name one thing you already keep or hand on — a way of doing something, a story, a phrase — and call it yours without softening it.
cells.core: The tuning is already happening — small adjustments to how something gets said, what gets kept, which version of it survives the next telling. It runs in ordinary moments and you'd describe it as just how things are. The adjustment is going; the recognition that you're the one turning the dial isn't.\n\nThat isn't modesty. It's the mechanism mislabelled as background. What you'd call the way things are, someone else would call a choice about what carries forward and what doesn't. Leaving it unnamed costs you the ability to tell when the tuning is off, since you've kept the dial at arm's length. The ask is to point at one thing you already pass on and call it yours, without handing the credit to the times or the family or the way it's been done.
cells.sheetLine: The tuning is already running. The dial is yours to hold.

The ask stays useful if I'm wrong about the setting, because the act is narrow enough to do in any room. The sentence that serves me more than them is any version of 'you are the one carrying the meaning forward' — it flatters a role rather than naming a moment.
